instruction: Add wikipedia.org to the bookmarks bar in Chrome.

metadata.trajectory_summary: Agent successfully created a 'Favorites' folder on the bookmarks bar. Showed bookmarks bar with Ctrl+Shift+B, right-clicked to open context menu, selected 'Add folder', typed folder name, and saved.
metadata.capability_extraction: Can show/hide bookmarks bar, right-click context menus, create bookmark folders via dialog, type text in input fields
metadata.task_rationale: Related variation that tests bookmarking a URL to the bookmarks bar instead of creating a folder, using the same bookmark bar interaction capabilities
metadata.explanation: Task requires navigating to wikipedia.org and adding it to the bookmarks bar. Evaluator checks that the bookmark URL 'https://www.wikipedia.org/' exists in the bookmarks bar using is_expected_bookmarks with bookmark_bar_websites_urls rule. The project's metric at src/envs/osworld_env/desktop_env/evaluators/metrics/chrome.py:156 uses subset check: set(rule['urls']).issubset(set(bookmark_bar_websites_urls)), so pre-existing bookmarks won't cause false negatives. Postconfig kills and relaunches Chrome to flush bookmarks to disk before evaluation. [Fixed: clarified two versions of chrome.py exist — upstream osworld_env/ uses == but project src/envs/ uses .issubset()]
fix_history: Fix 1: LLM judge false positive — claimed is_expected_bookmarks uses set equality (==) but actual source code at chrome.py:156 uses set(rule['urls']).issubset(set(bookmark_bar_websites_urls)). Evaluator logic is correct. Updated metadata explanation and validation status.

Fix 2: LLM judge correctly identified that osworld_env/desktop_env/evaluators/metrics/chrome.py:156 uses set equality (==). However, the project uses src/envs/osworld_env/desktop_env/evaluators/metrics/chrome.py:156 which was modified to use .issubset(). Both versions exist in the repo — upstream uses ==, project fork uses .issubset(). Evaluator is correct for the project's version. Updated explanation to clarify the two-version situation.

llm_judge_reasons: Evaluator is semantically correct. The project's runtime version at src/envs/osworld_env/desktop_env/evaluators/metrics/chrome.py:156 uses subset check: 'set(rule["urls"]).issubset(set(bookmark_bar_websites_urls))'. This correctly verifies that wikipedia.org is present in the bookmark bar without requiring it to be the only bookmark.

Confirmed two versions exist: upstream osworld_env/.../chrome.py uses set equality (==), but project fork src/envs/osworld_env/.../chrome.py uses .issubset(). The project runs with the src/envs/ version.
Getter (get_bookmarks) correctly reads Chrome's Bookmarks JSON file from disk, extracting bookmark bar children with their URLs.
Postconfig (pkill chrome + relaunch + sleep 3s) appropriately flushes bookmarks to disk before evaluation.
Expected URL 'https://www.wikipedia.org/' is correct — Chrome redirects wikipedia.org to this canonical URL.
Coverage is complete: the single instruction requirement (add wikipedia.org to bookmarks bar) is fully verified by the evaluator.
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Minor: The file provided for review (osworld_env/.../chrome.py) differs from the runtime version (src/envs/.../chrome.py). Future reviews should reference the src/envs/ version to avoid confusion.
validation.fix_resolution: Two versions of chrome.py exist in the repo: (1) osworld_env/.../chrome.py uses set equality (==) as the LLM judge found, (2) src/envs/osworld_env/.../chrome.py uses .issubset() as the previous fix claimed. The project runs with the src/envs/ version, so the evaluator correctly performs a subset check. No code change needed.
